feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — A citation is a symbolic reference, not a bounded material item.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — A designed convention embedded in scholarly systems.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not inspired by biological models.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Not a physical or architectural component.
feedback.Observable: Included — Must be seen to perform its function; often formatted and surfaced intentionally.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Can appear in text or screen but not defined by a particular medium.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires use and context to activate meaning.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Constructed purposefully to encode attribution and connection.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Does not independently generate outcomes.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Influences interpretation but not itself state-altering.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Included — Digital citations are clickable links; they prompt user engagement.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Used by systems but not embedded as modules.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Requires authorship and contextual use.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Other forms of attribution exist without citation format.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Represents another intellectual object or contribution.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Communicates deference, relevance, lineage, or critique.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Structured according to formal citation standards (APA, MLA, Chicago).
feedback.Compositional: Included — Contains distinct, nested parts (author, year, title, etc.).
feedback.Normative: Included — Subject to expectations and penalties; citation is a norm-enforcing practice.
feedback.Meta: Included — Its only function is to refer to other works.
feedback.Temporal: Excluded — May contain dates but is not a time-based system itself.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Stored, rendered, and managed through digital media.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists through shared cultural and disciplinary conventions.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Governed by editorial policies, academic codes, and scholarly bodies.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Citations contribute to author reputation and scholarly lineage.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Citations are enforced via peer review, software checks, and misconduct investigations.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Drives hiring, promotions, grants, and journal prestige.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Citation justice and bias are highly debated academic concerns.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Repeated in formalized ways across disciplines and formats.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Plagiarism, erasure, and misattribution carry ethical weight.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the academic citation as a symbolic, structured, and interactive scholarly artifact. It is both meta-referential and normative, situated at the intersection of ethics, authority, and institutional power. It functions as visible, rule-governed metadata that structures intellectual discourse and value across digital academic systems.
